question: What evidence supports the layered structure of the Earth’s interior?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Seismic wave behaviour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Seismic waves** are vibrations produced by earthquakes or artificial explosions, which travel through the Earth’s interior.
 
• Analysis of **seismic wave behaviour** provides vital information about the **layered structure** of the Earth.
 
• There are two types of seismic waves: **Primary (P) waves**, which are faster and travel through solids, liquids, and gases, and **Secondary (S) waves**, which travel only through solids.
 
• The fact that **S-waves** do not travel through the **Earth’s outer core** confirms that it is made of liquid material.
 
• **P-wave refraction** and **velocity changes** indicate the presence of different layers such as the **crust, mantle, and core**.
